evals.prompt: What is the maximum travel distance for a sprinklered domestic corridor in Hong Kong?

The response does not include conversational preamble

evals.prompt: A subcontractor stopped paying workers and they threaten to stop work. The main contractor says our latest payment certificate proves wages were paid. What should the architect do?
evals.expected_output: Apply Caps. 55 and 57: identify employer/subcontract chain, preserve wage/attendance and notice evidence, refer to LD conciliation and assess statutory upstream wage liability and deadlines separately from contract certification.
assertions: Does not treat a payment certificate as evidence of payment to workers
Identifies potential principal/superior-contractor wage liability and checks written notice deadlines
Separates labour-dispute resolution from contract deductions and extension-of-time entitlement

evals.prompt: Our Hong Kong practice is sending an architect to a Mainland project for two weeks. Does Cap. 78 automatically require contract attestation? What facts are needed?
evals.expected_output: Check employer presence/business in Hong Kong, employee category and wages; distinguish every overseas assignment from the specific external-employer arrangement; attestation is before departure if applicable.
assertions: Does not apply Cap. 78 automatically to an overseas assignment
Asks for or identifies actual employer location/business and employee category/pay
Explains pre-departure written-contract attestation for covered arrangements

evals.prompt: A subcontract worker was admitted to hospital after falling during A&A in an occupied office. The contractor proposes to wait 14 days and send Form 2 only. The landlord controls the access stairs. Is that sufficient?
evals.expected_output: Identify separate Cap. 282 compensation and Cap. 509 workplace reporting, urgent serious-injury notification, employer and occupier control of access, and insurance evidence; no blanket conclusion that Form 2 discharges all duties.
assertions: Flags urgent Cap. 509 notification rather than waiting 14 days
Distinguishes compensation reporting from workplace notification and checks overlap conditions
Addresses employer and landlord/occupier control of access
Requires incident/medical and insurance records without certifying liability

evals.prompt: An asbestos-removal worker reports lung disease and another worker reports hearing loss after years of noisy work. Does our Cap. 400 noise assessment and OSHC training settle their compensation entitlement?
evals.expected_output: Separate Caps. 360 and 469 disease compensation and medical/occupational assessment from Cap. 400 community noise and Cap. 398 OSHC training; retain exposure/employment history and refer to the relevant claim bodies.
assertions: Separates pneumoconiosis/mesothelioma and occupational deafness compensation pathways
Does not use Cap. 400 compliance or OSHC training as proof of claim eligibility
Retains exposure/employment evidence and refers diagnosis/eligibility to relevant specialists or boards

evals.prompt: The contractor wants to use a newly installed builders' lift tomorrow, citing our permanent lift's Cap. 618 permit. What evidence do we need?
evals.expected_output: Classify temporary equipment under Cap. 470, distinguish builders' lift/tower platform from Cap. 618 lift, material hoist and suspended platform, and obtain installation examination/testing and EMSD endorsement plus owner/registered-party evidence.
assertions: Does not accept a permanent lift permit as authorisation for temporary builders' lift use
Identifies EMSD/Cap. 470 registered-party and examination evidence
Checks the required endorsement before use and continuing records

evals.prompt: A hospital fit-out includes a steam boiler and X-ray suite. We have EPD fuel-burning approval and want to order the apparatus now. What other gates affect the layout and programme?
evals.expected_output: Cap. 56 registration and Certificate of Fitness remain separate from Cap. 311 approval; Cap. 303 licence is required before relevant possession/activity, with specialist shielding and access/maintenance coordination.
assertions: Separates pressure-equipment registration/fitness from fuel-burning approval
Identifies Radiation Board licensing before relevant possession/activity
Requires specialist shielding and equipment-specific design rather than inventing clearances or lead thickness

evals.prompt: For an A&A contract worth HK$2 million, we plan to strip suspect asbestos, pump muddy water to a storm drain and send all waste to a public fill facility. Our EIA permit is approved. What needs changing?
evals.expected_output: Apply Caps. 311, 354 and 358 independently: investigate suspect asbestos with registered specialists, identify chemical waste/authorised destinations, open the contract-specific waste account, and license/treat controlled runoff before discharge.
assertions: Does not treat the EIA permit as replacing air/asbestos, waste or discharge controls
Does not assume muddy runoff is exempt unpolluted water
Separates asbestos/chemical waste from inert public fill and requires appropriate disposal evidence
Identifies the contract-specific construction-waste account requirement

evals.prompt: A waterfront project near Deep Bay includes an outfall, dredging, sea disposal and temporary barge anchoring possibly inside a marine park. Is planning permission enough to mobilise?
evals.expected_output: Screen Cap. 127 authorisation, Cap. 313A navigation notice/directions, Cap. 466 dumping permit distinct from allocation, Cap. 476 activity controls, Ramsar/WCA/WBA boundaries and local planning/EIA requirements; verify actual designation and permits.
assertions: Separates foreshore, navigation and dumping gates from planning permission
Does not treat disposal allocation as a dumping permit
Checks marine-park activity restrictions rather than assuming a general permit authorises dredging
Distinguishes Ramsar treaty context from local statutory controls and checks actual boundaries
Qualifies old PNAP ADV-21 detail by source date

evals.prompt: We are replacing chillers with an imported HFC system, storing refrigerants and removing old CFC plant. Can we use the old Category 5 tank exemption and assume low ozone impact means the alternative is safe?
evals.expected_output: Apply Cap. 403 scheduled-HFC import/export and quota controls, controlled-refrigerant recovery rules, and current Cap. 295E/G classification and authority/exemption assessment; separately screen flammable/toxic alternatives and Cap. 51 gases.
assertions: Recognises scheduled-HFC controls effective from December 2025
Does not apply historical Category 5 exemptions as the current DG classification test
Requires substance/inventory and authority assessment including the Cap. 51 boundary
Checks applicable approved recovery equipment and separate refrigerant safety

evals.prompt: A MiC delivery will cross a rural watercourse on a new temporary culvert. We have a TMP and a TD 298 movement permit. Can the loaded wide vehicle go ahead?
evals.expected_output: Check Cap. 374 loading/route and relevant long/wide-load permits separately from TD 298/TMP; establish Cap. 446 main-watercourse designation and DSD consent before culvert works, plus Cap. 28 excavation permission where public road opening is involved.
assertions: Does not treat TMP or movement permit as a universal wide-load authorisation
Identifies TD long/wide-load permit assessment and actual route conditions
